integration_decision.name: CORRECT_CROSS_FILE_GENERATION_ORACLE_TO_PER_PATH_SNAPSHOTS
integration_decision.finding: The prior shorthand 'three-file generation hashes' must NOT compare hashes across latest.json, audit_latest.json and anata_latest.json: these files intentionally contain different schemas. Correct oracle is a B-publication snapshot for EACH path, compared to that SAME path after A resumes. The exact runner writes latest, audit, anata in sequence with no run-wide generation lock; storage.atomic_write_json atomically replaces one destination only. This is a source-level test gap, not a reproduced defect.
no_network_contract: Spawn child A using multiprocessing.get_context('spawn'); inside A, patch runner.atomic_write_json (not storage module or parent). Let A write latest.json and audit_latest.json, then pause BEFORE anata_latest.json; emit A_AT_HANDOFF_WRITE and fail closed on release timeout.

After A_AT_HANDOFF_WRITE, append one PIT-visible rowB to observations.jsonl; start child B on same local_dir, network=False, same as_of_ms; require B completed and persisted rowB in anata_latest.json before A release. If B cannot publish before A release, mark INCONCLUSIVE unless an explicit serialization witness is obtained; never infer PASS.

Before releasing A, capture SHA-256 independently for each of latest.json, audit_latest.json and anata_latest.json, and B's rowB identity/provenance; do NOT compare different file hashes to each other.

Release A; bound child exits and clean up on failure; compare each final path hash against its own B snapshot. Any overwritten B handoff and lost rowB is RED, with final mixed-generation path map recorded; matching all B snapshots is necessary but not by itself proof of general concurrency safety.

Run recovery child C, verify all three outputs parse and returned latest/anata equal their persisted counterparts, and rowB scoring provenance survives; then run targeted pytest and full python -m pytest -q part2/capital_flow/tests on exact-SHA checkout.
